**Finding: deviation (MFN — medium, commercial)**

- **§ 7.2 (p0026)** imposes a reverse MFN / right-of-first-refusal on us: we must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive before engaging another provider. It is open-ended — no defined product, no term limit, no reasonable-comparison carve-outs — and sits close to the playbook walk-away.
- It also directly contradicts **§ 12.3 (p0044)**, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment.
- No Vendor-granted MFN appears anywhere in the document, so nothing beneficial to us is lost by removal.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** delete § 7.2 in full, with a comment noting the wrong-direction problem, the § 12.3 conflict, and offering the fallback (single defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) if Vendor needs something in this space.
